study.title: Rupture risk assessment in cerebral arteriovenous malformations: an ensemble model using hemodynamic and morphological features

imaging.modality_detail: 2D DSA sequences (typically 4 fps) for time-density-curve hemodynamic features; 3D rotational angiography (3DRA) for nidus morphological features
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral arteriovenous malformation nidus; injections into internal carotid or vertebral artery

data_released.detail: Data available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Neuroradiologists blinded to hemorrhage status delineated nidus ROIs; hemorrhage confirmed by CT

task.task_description: Predict AVM rupture/hemorrhage risk using clinical features, nidus hemodynamic features from pixel-wise FFT-fitted DSA time-density curves (MIP, TTP, CBV, MTT, CBF) and 3DRA radiomic morphological features, with five ML models combined by weighted soft-voting ensemble; validated on a separate cohort for subsequent hemorrhage during conservative follow-up.
task.clinical_application: Rupture risk stratification of untreated cerebral AVMs to guide treatment decisions

temporal_evidence.quote: Time- density curves (TDCs) were fitted pixel- by- pixel, such that each pixel within the ROI generated a TDC

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Temporally separate same-center validation cohort (2008-2014, n=98, conservatively treated unruptured AVMs) for subsequent hemorrhage; authors state no external validation from independent cohorts

G1.quote: the construction of machine learning models requires a large number of cases to ensure stability

G2.quote: the single- center nature of this study limits its generalizability, as it lacks external validation from independent cohorts

G4.quote: the inherent two- dimensional nature of DSA sequences can lead to vessel overlap, making it challenging to provide the three- dimensional morphological features of the nidus accurately

G6.quote: Future research should include sufficiently large multicenter prospective studies to address these limitations.

G8.quote: The ensemble model effectively integrated multidimensional features

G11.quote: We addressed this limitation by including an additional validation dataset to evaluate the performance of the model in predicting subsequent ruptures in conservatively treated unruptured AVMs.

other_limitations: Validation cohort limited to conservatively treated unruptured AVMs (selection bias)
Small AVMs may present first with hemorrhage, potentially biasing size-rupture association
